source.title: Better Training using Weight-Constrained Stochastic Dynamics
source.authors: B. Leimkuhler; Tiffany J. Vlaar; Timothée Pouchon; A. Storkey

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own comparisons of test performance under constrained and unconstrained training, using a different intervention from the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study tests constrained training methods and reports test accuracy or validation loss against SGD baselines. It does not test random-label memorization, width sweeps, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, adaptive optimizers, batch-size penalties, dropout, magnitude-aware sharpness, or removing memorized examples. Prior-work statements are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study tests whether weight-constrained training improves held-out performance relative to selected SGD baselines. None of its experiments or arguments tests V1–V8. Decision-boundary curvature and prediction smoothness do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the classification conclusion: the authors present a constrained Langevin framework and report improved generalization from circle and orthogonality constraints relative to their unconstrained SGD and soft-constraint comparisons. Their supplementary language-model results explicitly qualify this advantage: carefully tuned SGD with weight decay outperforms c-CoLud.
record.recipe_differences: Uses custom constrained Langevin or SGD-style training rather than the interventions and measurements specified by the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcomes vary with constraint type and size, additive-noise temperature, hidden-layer count, step size, penalty strength, weight decay, and dataset. The paper reports the best spiral performance at τ = 5e-5; it also describes lower test performance for some temperature choices.

fits_no_version.finding: Circle and orthogonality constraints improve held-out performance over selected unconstrained SGD or soft-constraint baselines. Language-model gains reverse against carefully tuned SGD with weight decay: 4.77 versus 4.81 on Penn Treebank and 5.01 versus 5.09 on Wikitext-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Weight-constrained training can improve held-out performance, with benefits depending on workload and comparator tuning.

fits_no_version.finding: On the spiral task, the tested temperature producing the lowest estimated decision-boundary curvature also produces the best generalization performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decision-boundary smoothness can accompany improved generalization in constrained spiral classifiers.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021
record.problems: Several comparisons are shown only in figures without numerical values in the text. Some reported accuracy advantages are small. The study uses small run counts for several experiments; the 100-run spiral result does not report uncertainty for the cited accuracy comparison.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying outcomes were omitted. Cited prior-work results and theoretical statements were excluded from rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove penalties.
Dropout interventions, training-set-size dependence, and augmentation interactions.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, generalization-gap rankings, and comparison with norm or margin measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures and interventions do not test those versions; this does not dispute the reported method-performance differences. No omitted result bears on a listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening beyond interpolation; the MLP experiments vary depth, not width.
Convolutional versus fully connected comparisons and learned local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizer comparisons and tuning effects.
Large-batch generalization effects and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and their interaction with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness comparisons and correlations with the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.

rows.subject: 500-node single hidden layer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Train with constrained SGLD and compare with standard SGD on the spiral binary classification problem.
rows.note: The text explicitly gives these test accuracies as the constrained method versus standard SGD.
rows.check: Own-method performance comparison, outside V1–V8. The 91.7% versus 81% values accompany Figure 1; they are not explicitly reported as means over 100 runs. Figure 2 separately reports averaged results.

rows.subject: 100-node-hidden-layer MLPs with varying hidden-layer counts
rows.operation_detail: Compare orthogonality-constrained overdamped Langevin training with SGD variants on the 4-turn spiral dataset.
rows.baseline: SGD with standard initialization, orthogonal initialization, or orthogonal regularization; numerical values not stated
rows.note: The text says o-CoLod significantly outperforms the SGD variants for MLPs with more than 3 hidden layers.
rows.check: Own-method comparison varying depth, not V2's width beyond interpolation; ineligible as evidence for the listed versions.

rows.subject: ResNet-34
rows.operation_detail: Compare orthogonality-constrained underdamped Langevin training without weight decay with SGD-m without weight decay.
rows.baseline: SGD-m without weight decay; numeric value not stated
rows.note: The text describes the constrained method as strongly outperforming SGD-m without weight decay; the appendix describes the test-accuracy improvement as modest.
rows.check: Own-method comparison outside V1–V8. The modest accuracy improvement in Figure D10 concerns overdamped training, whereas this row concerns underdamped training in Figure 6; those descriptions should not be combined.

rows.subject: 1000-node single hidden layer perceptron
rows.operation_detail: Compare circle-constrained underdamped Langevin training with SGD-m and SGD-m weight-decay settings.
rows.uncertainty: Standard deviations included in the reported values
rows.note: The accuracy advantage over these baselines is small; the paper also reports improved test loss, but no numerical baseline test-loss values here.
rows.check: Own-method comparison outside V1–V8. Numerical accuracies match the text; the SGD baseline uses momentum 0.8.

rows.subject: small transformer with 2 encoder layers, 2-head self-attention and 200-node feed-forward networks
rows.operation_detail: Compare circle-constrained underdamped Langevin training with SGD-m.
rows.note: The table reports multiple SGD momentum settings separately; c-CoLud has a lower loss than each listed value.
rows.check: Constrained training versus momentum SGD does not test adaptive optimizers in V4. The reported advantage applies to baselines without weight decay; Table D3 reports tuned SGD with weight decay reaching 4.77, below c-CoLud's 4.81.
